title: Infinity Belize Project
subtitle: International private equity fund architecture, government relations, and capital campaign strategy for a sovereign-scale Caribbean development.
location: San Pedro, Belize / United States / international partners
summary: Bivines Group took 94 acres of undeveloped Caribbean beachfront - no concept, no structure, no investors, and no government relationships - and built the complete architecture for an $860M international private equity fund. Over 8 months, the work spanned three countries, five concurrent workstreams, investor materials, legal and transaction documentation, economic impact modeling, architectural coordination, and engagements at the Prime Minister level of the Belizean government. The capital campaign raised approximately $3M before reaching its $12M minimum viable threshold and was placed on hold.

carousel.title: 1. Overview
carousel.heading: From raw beachfront land to an $860M fund architecture
carousel.content:
Infinity Belize Project
San Pedro, Belize - June 2021-February 2022

We took 94 acres of undeveloped Caribbean beachfront - no concept, no structure, no investors, no government relationships - and built the complete architecture for an $860M international private equity fund from scratch. Over 8 months, we operated across three countries, produced the full suite of financial, legal, and campaign materials, and secured engagements at the Prime Minister level of the Belizean government. The capital campaign raised approximately $3M before reaching its minimum viable threshold and was placed on hold.

carousel.title: 2. Details
carousel.heading: $860M designed, ~$3M raised, $12M threshold unmet
carousel.content:
- Fund size designed: $860M (Infinity Belize Fund)
- Capital raised: ~$3M toward $12M minimum viable development threshold
- Projected fund returns: $5.4B profits - IRR 64% - MOIC 10.64x (4.5-year horizon, at full capitalization)
- Land: 94 acres, San Pedro, Ambergris Caye, Belize - acquired at $9.4M against $21M+ current market value
- Projected economic impact: $2.7B national impact - $142.5M gross corporate tax - 5,954 direct hospitality jobs
- Scope: 4,860 hotel keys - 12 hospitality structures - 4 water park complexes - airport - 16-mile railroad - ferry terminal
- Duration: 8 months - 3 countries - 5 concurrent workstreams
- Status: On hold pending capital mobilization

carousel.title: 3. The Situation
carousel.heading: A real opportunity with none of the infrastructure
carousel.content:
A private landowner held 94+ acres of beachfront property in northern San Pedro, Belize - one of the Caribbean's most sought-after development corridors. The land was raw. There was no concept, no development plan, no investor narrative, no entity structure, and no relationship with the Belizean government. There was a parcel, a vision, and a very large gap between them.

The client group understood that the opportunity was real. Belize had just installed a new government actively seeking public-private partnerships after COVID left the country with 68% unemployment and a mandate to rebuild its tourism economy fast. Caribbean land values were rising. US institutional capital was sitting at historic highs looking for ESG-aligned, DFC-insurable emerging market exposure. The conditions were right - but only for someone who could build the vehicle fast enough to take advantage of them.

The constraint was that none of the infrastructure for this deal existed. No entity, no structure, no term sheet, no investment thesis, no materials, no government contacts, and no capital relationships. We were not coming in to refine a deal. We were coming in to invent one - across three countries, with three different audiences, in parallel.

carousel.title: 4. The Ask
carousel.heading: Build the fund, deal, campaign, materials, and relationships
carousel.content:
The client needed a complete development finance strategy built from first principles. In practice, that meant:

- Build the fund: Design and model a sovereign-backed private equity vehicle capable of attracting US institutional investors through DFC
- Structure the deal: Author all transaction documentation for a cross-border real estate acquisition including escrow, contingent equity, and termination protections
- Create the campaign: Develop a phased capital campaign with conditional paths at multiple raise thresholds - not just a plan for success, but a plan for every outcome
- Produce the materials: Build a 20-slide investor deck, economic impact model, capital stack diagrams, and architectural massing program - everything an investor room or a government chamber would need to say yes
- Manage the relationships: Establish and navigate government engagements at the ministry, municipal council, and Prime Minister level
- Coordinate the team: Synchronize US legal counsel, Belizean compliance partners, UK-based architects, and seed investors across a single 8-month timeline

carousel.title: 5. The Approach
carousel.heading: Sequence sovereign credibility before the investor product
carousel.content:
The first strategic decision was sequencing: we chose to build the government relationship before building the investor product. In emerging market deals, sovereign credibility is not a late-stage validation - it is the foundation that makes the capital structure possible. DFC participation, political risk insurance, and institutional investor confidence all depend on documented government alignment. We went in-country first, which meant we could build the investor deck with proof of sovereign engagement already embedded, not promised.

The second decision was building for downside. Most capital campaigns are designed around a single success scenario. We built a conditional roadmap - four distinct development paths tied to four capital thresholds, from $750K to $12M+ - each with its own asset acquisition sequence, revenue strategy, and path to the next gate. This meant the project had optionality at every outcome level rather than a single point of failure. It also meant our investor conversations were honest about risk rather than optimistic about certainty.

The third decision was building the financial model and the space program simultaneously, rather than sequentially. The economic impact projections we needed for government audiences - 5,954 jobs, $2.7B national impact, $142.5M in tax revenue - required real inputs: actual building counts, key counts, square footages, and ADR assumptions. We produced the building-by-building space program first, which gave the financial model real numbers to work from, which gave the investor deck credible projections to present. The three documents were designed as a single integrated argument, not three separate outputs.

carousel.title: 6. The Work
carousel.heading: Fund modeling, deal structure, site programming, and government engagement
carousel.content:
Fund Architecture + Financial Modeling
We designed the complete capital structure for an $860M emerging market PE fund: a dual-bond debt instrument (Infinity Infrastructure Bond + Zone Bond) with a Belizean sovereign debt guarantee, DFC political risk and parametric hazard insurance, and a GP/LP structure with institutional investment banks as LPs and the Belizean Government as trustee LP. We modeled the fund across three portfolios (Infrastructure, Hospitality, Attractions), an 8-10 year liquidation horizon, and a second model built entirely for government audiences quantifying $2.7B in national economic impact.

Deal Documentation + Transaction Structure
We authored the full transaction suite for the 94-acre acquisition: land purchase summary and term sheet, staged escrow and earnest money structure, contingent equity provisions, non-compete protections, and a conditional decision-tree flowchart mapping every gate from offer execution through break-ground - including DFC trigger thresholds, MVDA milestones, and termination scenarios. We also produced the BGIC entity structure diagram and the full IBF capital stack diagram mapping 12+ entities and their contractual relationships.

Space Program + Architectural Coordination
We produced a building-by-building space program covering 12 hospitality structures (4,860 keys across three star ratings), 4 water park complexes, and four infrastructure projects including a 9,200-ft runway international airport, a 75,000 sf ferry terminal, a 16-mile railroad, and a $70M water plant. We coordinated with UK-based development firm Iterum to produce a 22-page massing document including site plans, isometric 3D views, use-type diagrams, and individual zone callouts for all 8 development zones across 100+ acres.

Capital Campaign Design
We designed a conditional fundraising strategy mapping four development scenarios - Blue Ocean ($12M+), Limited Development ($8M), Seed Development ($1.5M), and Media and Marketing ($750K) - each with corresponding asset acquisition steps and revenue strategies. The campaign targeted $12M in seed capital with a conditional path to $860M via DFC institutional raise. Approximately $3M was raised before the project was placed on hold.

Government Relations + In-Country Engagement
We led and participated in multiple in-country engagement sessions: ministry-level meetings, a formal presentation to the Belize City Council in official chambers, attendance and presentation at the Belize Investment Summit 2021 (a Government of Belize-hosted event), and a direct meeting with the Prime Minister of Belize to present the project and explore PPP alignment. All engagements required translating a private equity fund structure into the language of job creation, infrastructure investment, and national economic sovereignty.

carousel.title: 7. The Impact
carousel.heading: ~$3M raised and Prime Minister-level engagement secured
carousel.content:
We entered the engagement with nothing in place. In 8 months:

- ~$3M raised in seed and early development capital against a $12M target
- $860M fund structure fully designed and modeled - including capital stack, GP/LP waterfall, insurance instruments, and three-portfolio architecture
- Prime Minister-level engagement secured - direct meeting with the sitting Prime Minister of Belize to present the project
- Belize City Council presentation delivered in official chambers under the national seal
- Belize Investment Summit 2021 - presented from the Government of Belize podium alongside international investment community participants
- Multiple ministry-level meetings completed with area representatives and municipal officials
- $2.7B national economic impact projected (model-derived) - $142.5M gross corporate tax - 5,954 direct hospitality jobs
- Project status: On hold - $3M raised, below $12M MVDA threshold required to advance to DFC/3P infrastructure phase

carousel.title: 8. The Deliverables
carousel.heading: The full stack for investors, government, transaction parties, and architects
carousel.content:
- Investor Deck (20 slides) - Full investment narrative for a greenfield $860M PE fund, built for simultaneous use with US institutional investors and Belizean government audiences

- Infinity Belize Project Deal Structure Diagram - 12-entity capital stack showing sovereign debt guarantee, dual bond structure, DFC insurance instruments, GP/LP waterfall, and $5.4B profit pool

- BGIC Entity Structure Diagram - Entity-level ownership and contractual relationship map covering all joint venture parties, SPVs, shareholder agreements, and service agreements

- Land Purchase Flowchart - Conditional decision tree mapping every acquisition gate from offer execution to break-ground, including escrow triggers, MVDA milestones, DFC thresholds, and termination scenarios

- Property Owner Deal Summary - 5-page transaction summary and term sheet for the 94-acre cross-border acquisition, including earnest money structure, contingent equity provisions, and non-compete protections

- Fundraising Options Flowchart - Four-path conditional capital campaign roadmap mapping development scenarios to raise thresholds from $750K to $12M+, each with asset and revenue sequences

- Space Program - Building-by-building development specification: 12 hospitality structures (4,860 keys), 4 water park complexes, and 4 major infrastructure projects with square footages, level counts, and amenity programs

- Structural Architecture Master Plan (22 pages) - Full-site massing document including isometric 3D renders, use-type site plans, section drawings, and individual zone callouts for all 8 development zones across 100+ acres, coordinated with UK architecture partner Iterum

- Economic Impact Model - Government-facing financial model projecting $2.7B national economic impact, $142.5M corporate tax revenue, and 5,954 direct hospitality jobs derived from space program inputs
